recipe.name: Basketball — short native-video demo
recipe.description: A short real-game preview using continuous-video classification. This demo recipe prioritizes model evidence over noisy audio/motion proposal strength.

moment_types.name: made_basket
moment_types.description: The subject (a player on the team described in the prompt) makes a two-point field goal: the ball passes through the hoop right after their shot, jumper, or putback. Do NOT count free throws, misses, or any basket made by the opposing team.

moment_types.name: three_pointer
moment_types.description: The subject (a player on the team described in the prompt) makes a shot from behind the three-point line — look for the shot arc and the reaction at the make. Exclude misses and any shot by the opposing team.

moment_types.name: layup_or_dunk
moment_types.description: The subject finishes at the rim with a driving layup, fast-break finish, or dunk. Exclude missed attempts and any finish by the opposing team.

moment_types.name: block
moment_types.description: The subject blocks or clearly alters an opposing player's shot with their hand — deflected or swatted away, not merely contested from a distance.

moment_types.name: steal
moment_types.description: The subject takes the ball from an opposing player — a pick-off or a strip — forcing a change of possession.

moment_types.name: rebound
moment_types.description: The subject grabs a missed shot out of the air, especially a contested board or an offensive rebound that keeps the possession alive.

subject_selector.value: the subject described in the runtime prompt
subject_selector.team_color: Identify the subject team from the jersey/scoreboard description in the prompt. Set subject_present=true only when a player on that team is making the play; set it false for any player on the opposing team, so the opponent's plays are never included.
subject_selector.description: Highlights for the team in light-blue jerseys; exclude the team in black. Only clearly visible live plays.

selection.coverage: spread across the whole game, not clustered in one segment

guardrails.privacy: never center or identify non-subject minors; keep the focus on the subject's live action
guardrails.grounding: never label a moment_type the vision scorer isn't confident about — degrade to a lower score rather than fabricate a play; when it is unclear whether a subject-team player made the play, mark subject_present=false.

acceptance: every clip shows a player from the team described in the prompt making the play
no clip's highlighted play is made by the opposing team
clips show real basketball plays (basket, three, layup/dunk, block, steal, rebound), not padding
plays are spread across the whole game and not clustered in one segment
no clip shows a timeout, bench sequence, dead-ball standing around, warm-ups, or shaky camera work
